method: Walked the install, offline first-run, skipped-version upgrade, local authoring, signature admission, explain, and fixture-less rule flows as end-to-end state machines. Traced every dependency to its named current source and looked for a user who cannot complete the promised flow.

resolves.B-DL-01: OPEN-BLOCKER: local path authoring needs unsigned development content while DL-03 and the 'same admission' rule refuse every unsigned bundle.
resolves.B-DL-02: OPEN-BLOCKER: the air-gap/migrator path is explicitly unsolved, so full offline upgrade and user-custody compatibility cannot both be claimed.
resolves.B-DL-03: OPEN-BLOCKER: ARCH.INSTALL-UNIT has no cited architecture claim, threat dependencies point to superseded v1, and open P-1/P-2 are omitted despite the artifact assuming a contribution ecosystem.
resolves.B-DL-04: OPEN-BLOCKER: optional TypeScript/Rust providers conflict with the hard two-deep-language product promise unless install profiles and the meaning of 'full analysis' are specified.
resolves.B-DL-05: OPEN-BLOCKER: signing rules omit trust-root distribution/rotation, rollback/freeze and mix-and-match protection, revocation, and offline verification metadata.
resolves.B-DL-06: OPEN-BLOCKER: universal typed explain traces are not defined for imperative, built-in graph, scanner, and negative/relationship rules and conflict with retention/privacy limits.
resolves.B-DL-07: OPEN-BLOCKER: a fixture-less unverified rule may still affect a gate; admission and policy authority are not separated.
resolves.B-DL-08: OPEN-BLOCKER: no supported platform assignments or Rust substrate exist, so several conformance statements have no test domain.
resolves.B-DL-09: OPEN-BLOCKER: the conformanceTests are prose assertions with no schema, fixtures, runner, or negative controls.

evidence: localLoop requires loading a contribution from a local path with no registry involvement
localLoop requires the same admission/capability/validation path as a published bundle
DL-03 requires any unsigned contribution to be refused before execution
no development trust root, ephemeral signature, or explicit unsigned-dev grant is defined
findings.impact: A new author cannot run the first local rule without possessing a publication signing path, or the implementation must silently bypass the supposedly identical admission path.
findings.requiredChange: Keep one validation/capability pipeline but parameterize provenance policy. Add an explicit local-development grant bound to canonical path/digest and visible in PlanId; it may waive publisher signature only, never schema/capability validation, and cannot satisfy a production lockfile without explicit promotion/signing.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A specified local signing/trust mechanism already intended by 'same admission'.

findings.evidence: airGap says migrators must ship in the release but acknowledges unbounded history; VERSIONING requires user-custody migration/support windows; knownLimitations says the conflict is unsolved.
findings.impact: An air-gapped user who skipped beyond the bundled chain can neither open/upgrade evidence nor fetch the required bridge, violating either offline usefulness or compatibility.
findings.requiredChange: Choose a bounded contract: publish exact supported source majors; include the bounded migrator chain in each release or a separately signed offline bridge bundle; retain a read-only legacy inspector where promised; outside the window return a typed refusal naming signed intermediate bundles. Never promise arbitrary-history migration.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A versioning policy proving every supported offline upgrade path is finite, packaged, signed, and tested.

evidence: repository search finds no architecture/00 claim that one install may contain several signed artifacts
TM.F1 and TM.ADV4 cite superseded threat-model.v1
P-1/P-2 leave the third-party ecosystem and contribution ontology open
delivery nevertheless commits to contribution bundles, registry-independent overrides, signing, authoring, and first-party dogfooding
findings.impact: The artifact presents conditional product surface as a closed delivery design and inherits security terms from a rejected threat center.
findings.requiredChange: Make install-unit a candidate decision owned here; replace threat dependencies with v3 properties; add P-1/P-2 and branch contribution delivery as conditional until product disposition.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Resolvable current sources and a product disposition adopting the ecosystem.

evidence: P-4 and architecture/01 say TypeScript and Rust receive deep semantic providers
artifactSet marks both provider artifacts optional and says absence degrades to syntax
airGap and DL-01 promise full analysis offline on a supported language
'one install command produces a working tool' does not say which capability profile it installs
findings.impact: The same TypeScript/Rust install can be described as fulfilling or not fulfilling the product's strategic-depth promise.
findings.requiredChange: Define named install bundles/profiles and their capability manifests. The default product install must explicitly include or exclude each deep provider; 'working' and 'full analysis' must resolve to declared relations/Coverage, not marketing adjectives.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A product decision that strategic depth is available-but-not-default and a loud install-time capability contract reflecting that.

findings.evidence: The host verifies a signature and digest, but the artifact does not define trusted metadata, root-key bootstrap/rotation, expiry, revocation, anti-rollback/freeze, cross-artifact version-set consistency, or offline verification material.
findings.impact: A validly signed old/vulnerable artifact or incompatible mix of signed host/provider/grammar assets can pass the stated rules; key compromise recovery is undefined.
findings.requiredChange: Define a signed release manifest/version set with threshold/offline root trust, delegated artifact keys, expiry/rollback counters, rotation/revocation procedure, offline verification bundle, and atomic install/admission of one compatible set. Record the exact set in PlanId/Run provenance.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A referenced distribution-security specification providing these semantics.

evidence: explain requires per-filter candidate counts for any rule that did not fire
the architecture includes declarative rules, imperative rules, graph algorithms, external scanners, aggregate and negative predicates
retention T1 does not retain a proof/trace model for relationship or negative findings
candidate counts and symbols can themselves be sensitive and large
findings.impact: Some rule forms cannot produce the promised trace, and retaining it can violate privacy/volume budgets.
findings.requiredChange: Define an ExplainTrace union per evaluator class with required common states and typed optional proof events. For declarative IR, filter counts may be available; for opaque scanners/imperative code require a bounded producer trace contract or explicitly report unsupported. Tie durable trace availability to the proof-retention tier and privacy budget.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A universal evaluator instrumentation contract that can generate the listed trace without exposing source or unbounded state.

findings.evidence: DL-11 admits fixture-less rules and merely labels them unverified; extensions own detection but project policy can still map their findings into a required gate.
findings.impact: An uncalibrated rule can block CI while the delivery artifact calls admission successful.
findings.requiredChange: Separate installation/admission from policy eligibility. Default policy must not allow an unverified contribution to become required/blocking without an explicit tracked override; show verification state in plan, run, and explain output.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A policy-boundary rule elsewhere already forbidding unverified findings from gating.

evidence: platformMatrix assigns no OS/architecture to supported
P-4a leaves Rust substrate, redistributability, toolchain pinning, and execution behavior unresolved
DL-01, DL-02, DL-05, DL-06, and DL-12 require those choices
findings.impact: The artifact cannot instantiate its own offline, packaging, or platform tests.
findings.requiredChange: Keep distribution candidate until at least one vertical supported platform/language bundle and the Rust substrate decision exist; parameterize tests over a published matrix and artifact manifest.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Concrete platform assignments and provider artifacts.

findings.evidence: DL-01..12 are natural-language assertions only; no field schema, fixture references, runner, or recorded failing mutation is included.
findings.impact: The JSON is structured prose rather than a machine-checkable delivery contract.
findings.requiredChange: Attach executable fixture IDs/commands and expected envelopes/artifact manifests; add negative controls for unsigned, rollback, network fetch, missing provider, local-dev grant, and explain-state confusion.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A validator or harness referenced by this artifact and available in the binding object set.

sealedPropertiesCovered.assessment: Direction is represented, but supported offline migration and full-provider install are unresolved.
Provider languages are reflected; actual Rust substrate and default install capability remain open.
DL-12 requires an explicit grant but does not define the enforcement substrate.
The air-gap migration obligation is acknowledged but not discharged.
Fixture-less admission needs an explicit restriction before unverified detection can control a gate.

knownLimitations: This review does not choose a concrete signing framework or platform matrix; it specifies the security semantics those choices must satisfy.
P-1/P-2 may remove much of the third-party authoring surface; that would require narrowing rather than completing several findings.
The Rust packaging conclusion cannot be finalized before P-4a.
whatWouldChangeOverallVerdict: A v2 with an explicit local-dev trust mode, bounded offline migration chain, current/valid dependencies, named install capability profiles, complete signed-metadata lifecycle, evaluator-specific explain contracts, policy restrictions for unverified rules, a concrete vertical platform/provider bundle, and executable negative controls.
